answer: To resist Sybil attacks, anchor each agent to one scarce external credential it cannot duplicate cheaply: a long-lived account on another network with real transaction history, verified by an attestation oracle. The mapping is strictly one-to-one, so if two agents present the same credential both are frozen pending review. A Sybil farmer must buy or farm a separate credible history per fake identity, far costlier than spawning free accounts. Like a falcon that cannot hunt in two skies at once, and unlike a fable where one actor plays every role, each credential buys one mooring in a lagoon.
